title: Finite presentation of a module is local for an etale neighbourhood
statement: Let $g:(X',x')\to(X,x)$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism] inducing an isomorphism on the residue fields at the marked points [def-weil-residue-field]. For a quasi-coherent module $\mathcal M$ on $X$ [pqf-def-coherent], $\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation on some open neighbourhood of $x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] if and only if $g^*\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation on some open neighbourhood of $x'$.

source.place: Tag 057T, proof of (1)⇔(4), using Modules Tag 01PC and Descent Tags 02L2 and 03C4 together with Morphisms Tag 03WT.

proof.text: Assume $\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation on an open $U\ni x$. Apply lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation to $g_U:g^{-1}(U)\to U$ and $\mathcal M|_U$. The composition and tensor formula of def-pc-module-pullback identify $g_U^*(\mathcal M|_U)$ with $(g^*\mathcal M)|_{g^{-1}(U)}$: both are the tensor pullback of the same restricted sheaf along the restricted ring-sheaf map. Since $g(x')=x$, the inverse image $g^{-1}(U)$ contains $x'$. Thus $g^*\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation on a neighbourhood of $x'$.

Conversely, let $U'\subseteq X'$ be an open neighbourhood of $x'$ on which $g^*\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation. By lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map, $W=g(U')$ is open in $X$, and $x\in W$. Factor the restricted morphism as $U'\xrightarrow{q}W\hookrightarrow X$. The composite $U'\to X$ is etale, since the inclusion $U'\hookrightarrow X'$ is an open immersion and etale morphisms compose; $W\hookrightarrow X$ is etale as well. The cancellation clause of lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation therefore makes $q$ etale. It is surjective by the definition of $W$.

source.place: Tag 057T, paragraph beginning “The etale morphism g is open”; Morphisms Tags 03WT, 02GP, 02GN and 02GW.

proof.text: The singleton family $\{q:U'\to W\}$ is an fpqc covering, even though $q$ need not be quasi-compact. Indeed $q$ is flat by def-weil-etale-morphism. For any affine open $V\subseteq W$, put $U'_V=q^{-1}(V)$. The restricted map $q_V:U'_V\to V$ is surjective and etale: its composite with the etale open immersion $V\hookrightarrow W$ is the composite of $q$ with the etale open immersion $U'_V\hookrightarrow U'$, so apply etale composition and cancellation once more. By lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement, finitely many affine opens $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq U'_V$ have images covering $V$. They are also affine opens of $U'$. These are exactly the finite affine refinements required in def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering for the family $\{q\}$.

source.place: Tag 057T, the etale covering U\prime to g(U\prime); Topologies Tag 0218 (lemma-etale-affine) and Definition 022B (definition-fpqc-covering).

proof.text: The restriction $\mathcal M|_W$ is quasi-coherent, since the affine-local condition in pqf-def-coherent restricts to opens. By the tensor formula and composition identification in def-pc-module-pullback, $q^*(\mathcal M|_W)\cong(g^*\mathcal M)|_{U'}$: pulling back along $U'\to W\to X$ or along $U'\to X'\to X$ uses the same composite ringed-space morphism. This pullback is of finite presentation by the choice of $U'$. Apply the finite-presentation reflection clause (2) of lem-pc-fpqc-descent to the fpqc covering $\{q\}$ established in Step 3. It gives finite presentation of $\mathcal M|_W$, proving the reverse implication. Neither direction used the residue-field isomorphism, but that hypothesis is retained in the statement.
